attempts.summary: Configured node1 (RHEL 7.9) so new user passwords must be at least 12 characters and use at least 3 character classes, enforced via pam_pwquality. Discovered and corrected a subtlety: pwquality's default per-class length credits (dcredit/ucredit/lcredit/ocredit=1) reduce the effective minlen floor when extra classes are present, so minlen=12 alone did not guarantee a hard 12-char minimum. Set minlen=12, minclass=3, and zeroed all four credit values in /etc/security/pwquality.conf so both constraints apply independently. Verified enforcement live via passwd for real test users, then performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured baseline boot_id, rebooted node1 with `shutdown -r now`, confirmed boot_id changed after the node came back, and re-verified the policy config and PAM enforcement survived and still work correctly post-restart.
